newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangling obtains 200 mln yuan loan.
newsitem.headline: Jiangling obtains 200 mln yuan loan.

text.p: The Industrial and Commercial Bank of China has agreed to extend Jiangling Motors Corporation Ltd a 200 million yuan loan to supplement the Shenzhen-listed firm's working capital, an official press report and a company spokesman said on Thursday.
The Securities Times said a lending agreement had been signed recently, and added that Jiangling expects to obtain the loan later this year.

Jiangling, in which Ford Motor Co has a 20 percent stake, was recently named by Beijing as one of the country's top 300 firms eligible to benefit from a series of preferential government policies, the newspaper said.

A company spokesman said by telephone that Jiangling expected to receive 70 million yuan from the bank by the end of this year, with the remaining 130 million yuan to be disbursed in the first quarter of 1997.
He declined to provide details on the interest rate or maturity of the loan.
The official said Jiangling plans to channel the 200 million yuan into production of automobile engines.
Jiangling's results should pick up next year, when it projects output to reach 60,000 trucks and 120,000 engines annually, he said.

Jiangling said in its interim report for this year that under Chinese accounting standards, its audited net earnings plunged to 3.39 million yuan in the first half of 1996 from 14.96 million yuan in the year-earlier period.
The spokesman said the sharp decline was due to sharpened competition in mainland China's automobile sector and to Beijing's credit clampdown.
